decision: routed the rewrite through a bespoke figure-it-out run on branch rewrite/exact
why: the job spans four platforms and the owner reviews it after stepping away
result: open

decision: cloned expo/exact at 3baa28f beside the repo and installed pinned Bun 1.4.2 side by side
why: Exact has no packaged CLI and apps refer to the checkout by path
result: done

decision: found that this Mac can build Exact for web and macOS, needs SDK pieces for Android, and cannot build iOS
why: exact setup --check says the iOS host needs the iOS 27.1 SDK and this Mac has Xcode 26.1.1
evidence: exact setup --check --platform ios output in session transcript
result: iOS blocked until Xcode 27.1 is installed

decision: inventoried the Swift app before touching it
why: so the rewrite keeps every working feature and drops the stubs on purpose
result: done, summary generation and markdown notes turned out to be stubs

decision: researched current local models and picked three tiers
why: Whisper turbo at 1.6 GB is no longer the best size for quality trade
result: Lite Moonshine+Qwen3.5-0.8B, Balanced Parakeet v3+Qwen3.5-2B, Quality Granite Speech+Qwen3.5-9B, speeds unconfirmed

decision: chose one engine seam with a page module on web and native modules elsewhere
why: Exact runs app.ts on Hermes with pure JS only, so inference must sit behind native.later
result: open, to be proven by two spikes

decision: moved the Swift app under legacy/macos-swift and deleted the tracked 17 MB debug.log and default.profraw
why: the repo root becomes the Exact app, and the Swift code stays only as reference for the audio tap and meeting detection ports
result: done

decision: scaffolded the Exact app at the repo root with bundle id com.alona.app
why: exact new builds and its two placeholder tests pass on web
evidence: bun exact.mjs test web: 2 passed, 0 failed
result: web loop proven

decision: turned Exact's feedback notes off for this project
why: notes go to an Expo server and project details must not leave the machine unasked
result: done

decision: started three parallel spikes as separate threads: browser inference, macOS native inference, Android host
why: each host's inference path is the riskiest unknown, and the three share no files
result: open

decision: modeled the meeting pipeline as a state machine that one idempotent advance() call moves forward
why: the Swift app kept its job queue in memory and lost it on quit; here each tick reads the stage, asks the engine about that job, and restarts it when the engine forgot it
result: 26 tests pass; two mutations each turned one test red

decision: skipped the architect design arena for the core types
why: the app is greenfield and the shapes are concrete after reading the legacy inventory and research, so parallel design candidates would not change them
result: skipped on purpose

decision: wrote the five screens in Contract with a demo engine behind the same seam the real engines will use
why: the UI and pipeline can be proven on every host before any model runs, and tests stay fast and deterministic
result: 3 Contract tests pass on web

decision: built tools/flows.mjs to drive each flow, assert state at checkpoints, and save a screenshot per step and a video per flow
why: Exact's Contract tests cannot grant the microphone permission, only scripted drives can, and the same script produces the screenshots and videos the owner asked for
result: 5 of 5 flows pass on web with the demo engine

decision: the flow runner caught a model-removal bug: a removed tier still showed as installed
why: the service trusted a finished download job instead of asking the engine what is on disk
evidence: core/service.ts tierState, core/core.test.ts 'a removed tier reads as not installed'
result: fixed, test added

decision: set the brand as moss and lichen greens on warm stone grays in app.tamber
why: the owner asked for an earthy gray-green, minimal look; platform controls stay native and only the accent and the app's own surfaces take brand colors
result: tamber check passes, light and dark captured

decision: ran Exact's verify on web and fixed its three largest-text clipping findings
why: verify checks light, dark, two sizes, the accessibility tree, a relaunch, and the largest text size, which my own tests do not
result: verify: clean, 3 tests, 0 findings

decision: macOS spike came back VERIFIED: sherpa-onnx and llama.cpp run inside an Exact macOS app through xcframeworks
why: the spike transcribed the fixture at 4.2 to 4.8 percent word error and generated notes at 100 to 200 tokens per second on this M2 Max, under heavy load
result: verified, with three findings logged next

decision: kept a 13-expression patch for Exact's Swift host so macOS builds on Xcode 26.1.1
why: Exact at 3baa28f does not compile on this Mac's Xcode; my first build log said 'swift failed (1)' while my command reported exit 0 because it printed the tail's status, so I now return the build's own exit code
result: macOS build exit 0 after the patch; installing Xcode 27.1 would remove the need for it

decision: changed the Lite speech model to Moonshine Base and the Quality speech model to Parakeet v3
why: the researched picks, Moonshine Streaming Small and Granite Speech, have no sherpa-onnx build, and one speech runtime across Apple and Android is worth more than the small accuracy gap
result: open: Granite Speech needs transcribe.cpp, not tried

decision: wrote the Apple engine as four Swift files and pinned every model file to a repository revision with size and SHA-256
why: the audio is read and resampled one second at a time so an hour-long meeting does not load 1.4 GB the way the Swift app did, and a download only takes its final name after its hash matches
result: Lite tier downloaded and verified in the app in about a minute

decision: ran the production macOS app end to end on real models with the speech fixture
why: the agent's recorder writes a synthetic tone, so I swapped the fixture in and used the new Transcribe again action
evidence: scratchpad agent-mac4.log and agent-mac5.log; state detail.segments and detail.aiNotes
result: transcript accurate, notes structured; the 0.8B model misattributes owners, which matches the Lite draft-quality label

decision: rewrote the notes format as prose instructions and taught the title parser to drop an echoed instruction
why: Qwen3.5 0.8B copied the template line 'a short title for the meeting' as its title
result: the same meeting now gets the title 'Launch date and bug fixes for mobile app'

decision: moved model files to Application Support/exact/com.alona.app/models
why: my first path was Alona/models, which on a case-insensitive disk is the old Swift app's folder and holds its 1.5 GB Whisper file
result: old file untouched, new models moved
